uncertainties.detail: Reported retained property is qualified, not a verified complete holding schedule. The 2025 transaction positively transfers brand and management contracts; it does not prove an all-property sale. Several named retained assets and recent control corroboration support the current Real Estate inference. Exact private equity, debt, sale proceeds and portfolio weights remain unknown. Group development values and third-party fund capital are not personal assets.

Investor is inferred from sustained private property allocation and reported retention under transferred management. Founder described the earlier platform but may not describe its present sold operations. Passive ownership is not inferred from silence, and the control filing alone would not justify an active wealth role. Stronger post-sale personal governance evidence could change the relationship.

The material founder-built fortune supports broad Self-made. Neither no inheritance reported nor university education proves an independent start. The detailed Property Week article was paywalled and its archived PDF unavailable; a loan narrative copied by an unverified biography website was not used to determine a subtype.

The 2011 Forbes date and present registry agree on the birth period. Cypriot nationality is added as secondary without assuming Russian renunciation. Monaco residence is an explicit registry fact, not a property-location inference. A reported Russian patronymic is not added without sufficiently strong primary naming evidence.

The two biographies describe durable historical achievements and practice. Future renovation promises, net worth, current ownership percentages, sensitive allegations and vessel details are excluded. long_biography.plain_text:
Property developer Kirill Pisarev built The Collection's accommodation business around wealthy travellers who preferred renting homes to buying them. He chose destinations by following his customers' travel habits, creating a network of villas and small hotels with services suited to longer stays. The approach linked property development to continuing management of the finished buildings.

At Maison Villeroy in Paris, he offered residences with kitchens and dining rooms alongside hotel service. During the pandemic, local guests could book a stay and have a restaurant meal delivered to their residence. The hotel's restaurant earned a Michelin star after its first year.
